_comment: Machine-readable mirror of _shared/complexity-scoring.md. That file remains the prose source of truth; this config is guarded against drift by tooling/lib/drift-guard.test.mjs.

scope.description: one line, one file, no ripple effects
a single file or component, self-contained
several files, or one full feature within a module
multiple modules or services, or a change with wide blast radius
cross-cutting, touching many systems or the project's core architecture

ambiguity.description: minor gaps, safe to fill with a stated assumption
real gaps that had to be asked about before this score was possible
still underspecified after asking — open-ended goal, no clear acceptance criteria
closer to "explore this space" than a defined piece of work

risk.description: fully reversible, isolated, no external dependency
hard to reverse (data, published artifacts, shared infra) or depends on another repo/team
production-impacting, security/data-loss potential, or blocked on external input
high-stakes and largely outside this run's control — coordination, compliance, irreversible risk

uncertainty.description: a quick look at the code/docs settles it
unfamiliar library, pattern, or codebase area — real investigation needed
the right approach isn't clear yet; multiple viable strategies exist
genuinely open — no known approach going in

gates._notesCaveat: The .note strings on these gate bands (especially taskLevel) mirror _shared/complexity-scoring.md's current task-level table verbatim, which still contains subagent-dispatch language superseded by this repo's active no-subagent policy. Do not treat .note as dispatch instructions until roadmap item subagent-strip-out rewrites the source doc; the drift guard will then force this file to resync automatically.

taskLevel.note: may optionally peel off strictly mechanical sub-pieces to haiku45 subagents run alongside it
no capped subagent owns a task this hard; still uses normal haiku45/sonnet5 subagent scaling for separable mechanical portions

test-feature-high-optimism.note: optimism 4-5, plan complexity 4-7 or no plan / no Complexity line

verify.note: zero-token deterministic script check, no model reasoning involved

_driftSnapshot.fourFactorsBullets:
- 1-2: one line, one file, no ripple effects
- 3-4: a single file or component, self-contained
- 5-6: several files, or one full feature within a module
- 7-8: multiple modules or services, or a change with wide blast radius
- 9-10: cross-cutting, touching many systems or the project's core architecture
- 1-2: fully explicit, one reasonable interpretation
- 3-4: minor gaps, safe to fill with a stated assumption
- 5-6: real gaps that had to be asked about before this score was possible
- 7-8: still underspecified after asking — open-ended goal, no clear acceptance criteria
- 9-10: closer to "explore this space" than a defined piece of work
- 1-2: fully reversible, isolated, no external dependency
- 3-4: reversible but touches shared code
- 5-6: hard to reverse (data, published artifacts, shared infra) or depends on another repo/team
- 7-8: production-impacting, security/data-loss potential, or blocked on external input
- 9-10: high-stakes and largely outside this run's control — coordination, compliance, irreversible risk
- 1-2: the approach is already known
- 3-4: a quick look at the code/docs settles it
- 5-6: unfamiliar library, pattern, or codebase area — real investigation needed
- 7-8: the right approach isn't clear yet; multiple viable strategies exist
- 9-10: genuinely open — no known approach going in
